experiment: E4-scVI: sampling and quality-control sensitivity of the deployed scVI dispersion contrast
question: Does the scVI shared-per-gene versus per-cell dispersion contrast (each against Poisson sampling on the model's own fitted mean) keep its direction across the eight E4 corpora?
corpora: the eight E4 corpora (reference, uniform seeds 1-3, cell-type floor, batch balanced, 10,000-cell cap, MAD quality control) as built by e4-sampling-sensitivity/build_corpus.py
model: scvi-tools 1.4.3 SCVI with gene_likelihood='nb', batch_key='dataset', package defaults otherwise (as in the original deployed comparison); dispersion 'gene' (shared per gene) and 'gene-cell' (per cell)
training: train split only; early stopping enabled; scvi.settings.seed = fit seed
inference: fitted mean and dispersion on test cells via get_likelihood_parameters(n_samples=10, give_mean=True)
draws: Poisson(mu) with numpy default_rng((seed, 2)); NB(mu, theta) with the shared sample_nb at seed + 1
endpoint: expressed-gene calibration error (primary endpoint) per dataset x cell-type group with >= 20 test cells; signed variance ratio reported descriptively
contrasts: shared per-gene NB minus Poisson calibration error
per-cell NB minus Poisson calibration error
inference_stats: seeds averaged within group, groups within dataset; equal-weight mean over datasets; 2000-resample dataset-cluster percentile bootstrap, seed 20261106; group-level Poisson-win fraction
stability_rule: a contrast is stable when its interval classification (below zero / spans zero / above zero) matches the reference corpus
retention: all corpora, seeds and signed effects retained; no outcome-based exclusion
not_run: energy-distance redraw sweeps of the original deployed comparison (primary endpoint only, to bound compute)
